It is one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} for Tabe Shrine, a shikinaisha of Kamo District, {{ill|Mino Province|ckb|پارێزگای مینۆ|cs|Mino (provincie)|de|Provinz Mino|es|Provincia de Mino|eu|Mino probintzia|fa|ولایت مینو|fr|Province de Mino|gl|Provincia de Mino|hak|Mî-nùng-koet|id|Provinsi Mino|it|Mino (provincia)|ja|美濃国|ko|미노국|lt|Mino žemė|nl|Mino (provincie)|pt|Província de Mino|ru|Мино (провинция)|simple|Mino Province|sk|Mino (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мино|th|แคว้นมิโนะ|tr|Mino (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Міно|vi|Tỉnh Mino|wuu|美濃国|zh|美濃國|zh_min_nan|Mino-kok|zh_yue|美濃國|qid=Q864156}}. Another theory identifies Tabe Shrine with {{ill|Tabe Shrine|ja|太部神社|qid=Q11444532}} in the same town. Its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was village shrine.

The annual festival on the second Saturday and Sunday of April is called the Tabekoten Shrine Festival, in which two {{ill|Matsuri float|bcl|Matsuri float|fa|سانشا (جشن)|ig|Matsuri sere n'elu|ja|山車|ko|다시 (수레)|ru|Даси (праздничная повозка)|simple|Matsuri float|zh|藝閣|qid=Q11470974}} are pulled.

== Overview ==
The founding date is unknown. It is said to have formerly been called Tabe Shrine and Tabekotenjin, and later to have merged Sugawara no Michizane.

In the Edo period, it was said to be the village guardian shrine and general shrine of Kawabe for Kawabe village, Ishigami village, Kashio village, and Tochii village (now the west-bank area of the {{ill|Hida River|fa|رود هیدا|fr|Hida-gawa|ja|飛騨川|no|Hida (elv)|ru|Хида (река)|th|แม่น้ำฮิดะ|uz|Hida daryosi|qid=Q3366160}} in Kawabe). Since Meiji, it has been the village guardian shrine of Nakakawabe and Nishitochii.

== Tabekoten Shrine Festival ==
*A festival transmitted since the Edo period. Two floats are pulled from Tochii Shrine to Tabekoten Shrine, and lion dance is dedicated in the precincts.
*At 6:00 a.m. on Sunday, the “sake-buying rite” is held. Early in the morning, a parishioner wearing the mask of “Haiō,” messenger of Tenjin, goes with the lion to a sake brewery and buys sake to offer to Tenjin.

Haiō appears wearing a mask (close to a {{ill|Tengu|ar|تينغو|as|টেংগু|az|Tenqu|azb|تنقو|bcl|Tengu|ca|Tengu|de|Tengu|eo|Tengu|es|Tengu|eu|Tengu|fa|تنگو (شینتو)|fi|Tengu|fr|Tengu (folklore)|fy|Tengu|gl|Tengu|hu|Tengu|hy|Տանգու (արարած)|id|Tengu|it|Tengu|ja|天狗|jv|Tengu (mitologi)|ko|텐구|la|Tengu|mk|Тенгу|mni|ꯇꯦꯟꯒꯨ|ms|Tengu|nl|Tengu|no|Tengu|pl|Tengu|pt|Tengu|ru|Тэнгу|simple|Tengu|sr|Тенгу|sv|Tengu|ta|தெங்கு|th|เท็งงุ|tr|Tengu|uk|Тенґу (міфологія)|vi|Tengu|zh|天狗 (日本)|zh_yue|天狗 (日本妖怪)|qid=Q742360}} mask but with a less prominent nose) wrapped with a shimenawa-like band. This resembles the fly-chasing man in the annual festival of {{ill|Abushina Shrine|ja|阿夫志奈神社|qid=Q11657364}}, also in Kawabe, said to represent {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|az|Sarutahiko|fa|ساروتاهیکو اوکامی|fr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|it|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|ko|사루타히코 오카미|mni|ꯁꯔꯨꯇꯍꯤꯀꯣ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|pl|Sarutahiko|ru|Сарутахико|simple|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ta|சருதாகிகோ அகாமி|tr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|zh|猿田彥|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}}.
